finding: CF-A-FINEST-TIER-IS-THE-NUMBER (Drew ruling 18, corrected against source, 2026-09-08). BCP states plainly that 1997 Finest's Bronze/Silver/Gold is a property of the CARD NUMBER, not a parallel axis crossed with it: 'there are not Bronze, Silver, and Gold versions of every card in the set... There are no Common/Bronze or Uncommon/Silver versions of card #342.' Ranges: Bronze 1-100 and 176-275, Silver 101-150 and 276-325, Gold 151-175 and 326-350; all 350 numbers were transcribed from BCP's six tier sections and every heading agrees with the range rule (zero mismatches). A plain 'Refractor' row is therefore an under-specified address: it names a card whose tier the number already fixes. Each entry RESLUGS such a row onto its number's tier Refractor, or RETIRES it where that tier row already exists. SCOPE IS DELIBERATELY NARROW: sport=baseball AND year=1997 AND setKey=topps-finest only. The year-less topps-finest key also holds 999 rows of 1997-98 Topps Finest BASKETBALL (Jordan, Duncan, Shaq), which is a real, separately-tiered product; not one basketball row is touched here. NOTE: an earlier draft of this list proposed retiring hiq:basketball:1997:topps-finest:325:gold-refractor and :101:bronze-refractor as 'wrong-tier baseball rows'. That was wrong - they are correct-tier BASKETBALL cards (Tim Duncan rookie year) whose only defect is sharing the year-less product key. They are excluded.
